sar-scope-review: Abstract, p.1: the authors state the modalities (MRI, CT, X-rays, histopathology) and tasks (classification, segmentation, reconstruction) their review covers, and that they compared QML with classical counterparts. Both quotes are in the same abstract passage.
sar-scope-four-modalities-vs-seven: Section I-C contribution 1, p.4, states the four modalities; Section III opening, p.12, states that the section covers MRI, CT, PET, SPECT, ultrasound, X-ray radiography and histopathology. Both are the paper's own scope statements, and the value reports both without merging them.
sar-two-categories-qml: Section I-B-1, p.4: 'There are two primary categories' followed by the two definitions with examples. The value matches the passage.
sar-qubit-definition: Section II-A, p.5: the authors define a qubit as the fundamental unit of quantum information, a vector in a two-dimensional complex Hilbert space (the quote is cut at the line break; 'Hilbert space [52]' follows). A definition the paper gives, so HIGH as a definition.
sar-entanglement-definition: Section II-A, p.5: the sentence is the authors' own definition of entanglement (cited to [54]). It is a loose definition (correlation 'regardless of the distance'), but the value says only that the authors define it so.
sar-vqc-components: Section II-B-1, p.7: 'The components of a VQC are:' followed by the numbered list of exactly six items named in the value. The quotes carry the first and last items; the passage carries the rest.
sar-qcnn-architecture: Section II-B-2, p.8: 'The architecture of QCNN is:' followed by four bullets (input, convolutional, pooling, fully connected). The value matches all four.
sar-metric-families: Section V-C, p.27: the authors state the metric set for their QML vs classical benchmark framework, summarized in Table 16 ('This unified benchmark'). The passage lists classification, segmentation and regression metrics plus hardware-aware efficiency indicators, as the value says. The quotes carry only the first two families; the passage carries the rest.
psi-influence-definition-informal: More on the mathematics, p.4: 'The conjecture concerns the influence of a bit: the average change in a polynomial's value when the bit is flipped'. It is the page's plain-words definition. The formal one on p.6 squares the change, so the plain-words version is informal.
psi-influence-definition-squared: Theorem passage, p.6: Inf_i(f) 'is the squared change from flipping bit i, averaged over all inputs as in the figure'. The figure caption on p.5 says the same: squared and averaged over all 16 inputs. It is the definition the theorem uses.
